fields.Front: What is Object-Oriented Design and Analysis (OODA)?
fields.Back: Designing a system using objects that represent real-world entities and interact to solve a problem, structuring the system to be modular, flexible, and easy to maintain.
Bundling data (attributes) and methods (behaviors) into a single unit (the object) and restricting direct access to some of the object's components.

fields.Text: {{c1::Inheritance}} allows one class to derive properties and behaviors from another class.
{{c1::Polymorphism}} allows one interface to be used for different data types or classes (e.g., function overloading, overriding).
Compile-time polymorphism includes {{c1::function overloading}} and {{c2::operator overloading}}.
fields.Extra: From the speaker notes on the Polymorphism advantage slide.

fields.Front: What are the three steps for designing classes and objects?
fields.Back: 1. Identify objects; 2. Define attributes and methods; 3. Determine relationships.

fields.Front: In an online shopping system, what candidate objects do the slides identify?
What attributes and methods might a Product class have?
Define association (Week 1) with the slide example.
fields.Back: Objects know about each other; e.g., a Customer has an Order.

fields.Front: Define aggregation (Week 1) with the slide example.
fields.Back: One object contains or is composed of other objects; e.g., an Order contains multiple Product objects.

fields.Front: Define inheritance as a relationship (Week 1) with the slide example.
fields.Back: One object is a specialized version of another; e.g., Admin and RegularUser inheriting from User.

fields.Text: Relationship types in OODA: {{c1::Association}} = objects know about each other; {{c2::Aggregation}} = one object contains others; {{c3::Inheritance}} = one object is a specialized version of another.
